principle: Parallel execution is safe only because graph construction already resolved dependencies and cycles first
because: The 9-phase construction in T-027 adds nodes, wires depends_on and interpolation edges, and validates a single acyclic root before any walk begins; T-028's depth-first-with-parallelism traversal and its default concurrency of 10 are only correct because that validation already happened - the concurrency knob is safe to turn precisely because it operates on a graph whose ordering constraints were proven, not assumed.

principle: A module built as a stable interface for a consumer who never opens its internals
because: Dependency inversion (T-012) and preconditions (T-013) exist so a module's consumer never has to open its internals to know what it needs or assumes; flat trees and shallow nesting (T-011, T-016) keep that contract traceable instead of buried in a chain; scoping by encapsulation, privilege, and volatility (T-015) draws the boundary so the interface doesn't leak scope it shouldn't; data-only modules (T-014) and shipping underspecified-but-over-exposed (T-017) are the same idea applied to reads and outputs; T-042 and T-049 are what building and then deliberately breaking that contract look like in practice.
